newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to continue monetary restraint in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to continue monetary restraint in 1996.

text.p: Malaysia will maintain its policy of monetary restraint for the rest of 1996, the Ministry of Finance said in its 1996/97 Economic Report released on Friday.
The report said despite ongoing monetary and credit restrictions, demand pressures remain strong.
The base lending rate increased to 9.35 at end August from 7.70/90 in August 1995, according to the report.
"In view of the risks for demand pressures for the rest of 1996, the present stance of monetary restraint will be maintained," the report said.
The report did not say if the policy would be continued into next year.
The report said broad money (M3) expanded by 21.8 percent year-on-year at end August this year against a 16.6 percent expansion last year.

Total deposits of commercial banks stood at 219.69 billion ringgit as of end August against 182.75 billion in August of 1995. Total loans stood at 201.48 billion against 160.65 billion in the same periods.
The ministry said the main thrust of central bank policy will remain on managing excess liquidity.

"BNM will monitor closely developments in credit and monetary growth, particularly lending for less productive activities. While ensuring that funds are utilised effectively, policy will concomitantly be aimed at the effective mobilisation of savings," the report said.
